features.name: Presidio PII Anonymization Pipeline
features.description: On-device PII anonymization using Microsoft Presidio + spaCy NER, integrated directly into the FastAPI backend. Anonymization happens at send-time (not storage-time): raw transcripts stay local and real; only context basket payloads sent to the AI panel are anonymized. Two-tier detection: Tier 1 (PERSON, EMAIL, PHONE, LOCATION, DATE, URL) replaced with realistic Faker surrogates; Tier 2 (SSN, CREDIT_CARD, PASSPORT, IBAN, BANK_NUMBER) hard-redacted to [TYPE] placeholders. features.name: Calendar Integration & Auto-Recording
features.description: Connect to Google Calendar and Outlook to detect upcoming meetings and auto-start recording when they begin. Microsoft uses same pattern, scope Calendars.Read via Graph API /me/calendarView

Phase 2 — Calendar polling: new CalendarContext.tsx with adaptive polling (5min idle → 60s approaching → 15s imminent). Use Google syncToken / Microsoft deltaToken for efficient incremental sync (only changed events). Both APIs auto-expand recurring meetings (Google: singleEvents=true, Microsoft: /calendarView endpoint)

Phase 3 — Auto-record trigger: CalendarContext detects meeting within configurable lead time (30s default), shows toast with cancel button, then calls existing recordingService.startRecordingWithDevices() with meeting title pre-filled from calendar event
Phase 4 — Auto-stop: on calendar end time + 2min grace period, or VAD silence > 3min (reuse existing pipeline.rs VAD), show 'Stop recording?' toast with snooze option
Phase 5 — Sidebar widget: NextMeetingCard component showing countdown, title, attendees. Placed above meetings list
Phase 6 — Settings: CalendarSettings component — connect/disconnect Google/Microsoft accounts, toggle auto-record per calendar, configure lead time (0/30/60s)
Phase 7 — Token storage: use tauri-plugin-store (encrypted) initially, migrate to OS keychain when F019 lands

features.name: Speaker Diarization (Who Said What)
features.description: Identify and label different speakers in the transcript. Without diarization, transcripts are a single undifferentiated stream — useless for meeting notes where 'who said it' matters. Use pyannote.audio for local on-device diarization to maintain the privacy-first promise. Speaker labels appear inline with transcript segments.
steps: ✅ Phase 1 — Install: Added pyannote.audio>=3.3.0 to requirements.txt. User still needs to pip install torch+torchaudio (CUDA) and pyannote.audio

✅ Phase 2 — Backend diarizer.py + db.py + main.py: Created diarizer.py service (model loading, GPU inference, transcript alignment). Added 4 DB tables (diarization_processes, speaker_names, speaker_profiles, meeting_speakers) + CRUD helpers. Added 7 API endpoints (/api/diarize/*) with background task processing
✅ Phase 3 — Alignment: Built into diarizer.align_with_transcripts() — midpoint matching with overlap fallback, UNKNOWN as last resort

✅ Phase 4 — Frontend: Added speaker_label to types, color-coded speaker badges in VirtualizedTranscriptView, speaker prefix in transcript chunks for AI context, pass-through in usePaginatedTranscripts and TranscriptPanel

✅ Phase 5 — Speaker naming UI + triggers: SpeakerNamingModal component, diarization settings in PreferenceSettings (HF token, model download, auto-diarize toggle), Identify Speakers button in meeting details, auto-trigger in useRecordingStop
✅ Recovery (2026-07-01) — Recovered the orphaned Phase 1-5 work onto feature/speaker-diarization (rebased off main, 3-way merge). Frontend tsc passes; backend py-compiles.

✅ Eval harness (2026-07-01) — audio_testing/diarization/: Word Speaker Accuracy scorer w/ optimal label mapping (self-tested), ElevenLabs ground-truth bootstrap, pyannote config-sweep loop. Supports mixed + channel-split (mic=LOCAL) modes. Target approach: channel split + pyannote on system channel.

⏳ Phase 5.5 — Runtime setup: Install pyannote.audio + torchaudio (torch already present), get HuggingFace token + accept community-1 terms, ELEVENLABS_API_KEY to bootstrap ground truth, then run the harness loop and test end-to-end on a real recording

Phase 6 — Voice fingerprinting: extract 192-dim embeddings via pyannote/embedding model, store in speaker_profiles table (BLOB). On new meetings, match unknown speakers against known profiles via cosine similarity (threshold ~0.75). Running average updates embedding over multiple meetings
Phase 7 — Export: include speaker labels in all export formats (F010). Add speaker filter to transcript search

features.name: Enterprise Readiness (SOC 2, SSO, Admin Console)
features.description: Enterprise buyers in regulated industries (legal, healthcare, finance) are the highest-value segment for a privacy-first tool, but they require SOC 2 certification, SSO/SCIM, admin controls, and audit logs before procurement will approve. This is the gate between 'interesting tool' and 'purchasable product' for enterprise.
steps: Phase 1 — Audit logging (no server needed, 2 weeks): append-only SQLite table with hash chain for tamper evidence. Log auth, recording, transcript access, AI queries, settings changes, exports. Structured JSON events with ULID IDs. SQLite triggers prevent UPDATE/DELETE. Periodic Merkle root for verification

Phase 2 — Data retention (no server needed, 2 weeks): retention_policies and legal_holds tables in Rust SQLite. RetentionEnforcer runs on startup + hourly. Legal holds override retention. Secure file deletion (zero-overwrite before unlink) for audio files. Configurable per-org policy

Phase 3 — SSO via OIDC + PKCE (requires server, 4 weeks): use `openidconnect` Rust crate (v4.x) for OIDC Authorization Code + PKCE. System browser auth (not embedded webview per RFC 8252). Localhost loopback redirect. Supports Okta/Azure AD/Google Workspace natively. ALTERNATIVE: WorkOS ($0.25/MAU) handles SAML+OIDC+SCIM as single API, eliminates months of IdP work

Phase 4 — Lightweight identity server (requires hosting, 3 weeks): new FastAPI service with PostgreSQL. Handles user directory, license management, device enrollment, policy distribution. Desktop app polls for policy updates (pull model — works behind firewalls). Revocation check on launch + every 15-30min

Phase 5 — SCIM (requires server, 2 weeks): SCIM endpoint on identity server receives user create/update/delete from IdP. Critical for deprovisioning — revoking access within minutes when employee leaves. ALTERNATIVE: WorkOS SCIM handles all IdP quirks

Phase 6 — Admin console (3-4 weeks): React SPA web dashboard. User management, policy editor (retention, AI usage, recording rules), audit log search/filter/export, device enrollment status, compliance dashboard

Phase 7 — SOC 2 audit (6-14 months total): engage GRC platform (Vanta $10-25K/yr for automated evidence collection), readiness assessment ($15-30K), Type 1 audit ($20-50K, 2-3 months), then Type 2 observation period (6 months) + audit ($30-80K). Total first-year: ~$75K-185K including engineering

implementation.architecture_decision: Data stays local on devices (privacy differentiator). Central server ONLY handles organizational metadata (users, policies, audit aggregation) — never meeting content. Hybrid model: 'compliance controls of centralized management + privacy guarantees of local data processing'

sso_libraries.rust: openidconnect v4.x (full OIDC RP with PKCE, discovery, token validation)
sso_libraries.shortcut: WorkOS ($0.25/MAU) — unified SSO+SCIM API across all IdPs

implementation.audit_log_schema: Structured JSON: {id (ULID), timestamp, event_type, severity, actor {user_id, email, device_id}, resource {type, id}, context {}, result, chain_hash, prev_hash}
implementation.retention_schema: Tables: retention_policies, legal_holds, meeting_legal_holds. Legal hold is additive — meeting only eligible for deletion when ALL holds released
implementation.server_requirement: SSO, SCIM, admin console, and audit aggregation ALL require a hosted server component. Cannot be fully local. MDM (Intune/Jamf) is a limited alternative for policy distribution only
implementation.total_budget: $150K-$250K including engineering, tooling, and audit fees
implementation.effort_estimate: Phase 1-2: 1.5 eng-months. Phase 3-6: 3 eng-months. Phase 7: ongoing support during audit

features.notes: The hard truth: to sell to regulated enterprises, you need a central server component. WorkOS ($0.25/MAU) can shortcut SSO+SCIM by 2-3 months. Start with audit logging + retention (no server needed) to build SOC 2 foundation, then add identity server + admin console.

features.name: Multi-Device Encrypted Sync
features.description: Sync meetings across devices (work laptop + home desktop) using end-to-end encrypted cloud storage. Server never sees plaintext — keys derived locally from passphrase. Thin relay (S3/MinIO) stores opaque encrypted blobs. Enables team sharing without sacrificing the privacy story.
steps: Phase 1 — Encryption layer: AES-256-GCM with keys derived from user passphrase via Argon2id. Encrypt meeting metadata, transcripts, summaries, AI conversations. Audio files optional (large). Use Rust ring crate.
Phase 2 — Sync protocol: content-addressed blobs (SHA-256 hash as key). Delta sync — only upload changed meetings. Conflict resolution: last-write-wins with merge for concurrent edits.
Phase 3 — Storage backend: abstract StorageProvider trait. Implementations: S3-compatible (AWS/MinIO/Backblaze B2), local folder (USB drive sync), WebDAV (Nextcloud). User configures in settings.
Phase 4 — Device pairing: generate sync key on device A, enter on device B. Key exchange via QR code or manual passphrase entry. No account creation needed.
Phase 5 — Selective sync: choose which meetings/date ranges to sync. Don't sync audio by default (bandwidth). Transcript + summary + metadata only.

features.description: Export meeting transcripts and summaries into a personal knowledge base. (2) Vector DB — embed transcript chunks into a local ChromaDB/Qdrant instance for semantic search across all meetings ('What did the Acme team say about pricing in any call?').

Phase 2 — Auto-sync to Obsidian: toggle in settings to auto-export every meeting on recording stop. Watches vault folder for conflicts.

Phase 3 — Vector DB ingestion: POST /api/knowledge/ingest endpoint. Chunk transcript into 200-word overlapping segments. Embed with a local model (nomic-embed-text via Ollama, or sentence-transformers). Store in ChromaDB (pip install chromadb, serverless local mode).
Phase 4 — Semantic search: 'Search all meetings' input in sidebar. Query the vector DB, return top-K matching segments with meeting title + timestamp + snippet. Click to navigate to that meeting.

Phase 5 — AI context enrichment: when using the AI panel, optionally pull relevant past meeting context from the vector DB and inject into the prompt. 'Based on your previous calls, the prospect mentioned budget constraints in 3 separate meetings.'

features.name: LLM Transcript Correction
features.description: Use a local lightweight LLM (Qwen2.5-1.5B via Ollama) to post-process Parakeet/Whisper output in real-time. Fixes grammar, spelling, homophones (their/there/they're), punctuation, and removes filler words (um, uh, like, you know). Parakeet is CTC-based and benefits enormously from LLM post-correction — the combination matches Whisper large-v3 quality at lower latency.
steps: Phase 1 — Correction service: new backend/app/transcript_corrector.py. TranscriptCorrector class using Ollama AsyncClient with qwen2.5:1.5b. Preload model on startup with keep_alive=-1 (permanent VRAM residency, ~1.2GB).

Phase 2 — Real-time pipeline: after each Whisper/Parakeet segment, POST to /api/correct with raw text + last 100 words as context. Debounce: accumulate 2-3 segments (~10s speech) for better homophone disambiguation. Timeout at 500ms, fall back to uncorrected text.

Phase 3 — Safety: reject hallucinated output if corrected text > 2x input length. Log correction diffs for debugging. Store both original and corrected text in SQLite (original_text + corrected_text columns).
Phase 4 — Settings: toggle correction on/off in Transcription settings. Model selector (qwen2.5:0.5b for speed, qwen2.5:1.5b for quality, qwen2.5:3b for best). Show correction latency stats.
Phase 5 — Rust-side option: for lowest latency, call Ollama HTTP API directly from transcription worker.rs, bypassing Python backend. Configurable in settings.
Phase 6 — Post-recording refinement: after recording stops, run a second pass over full transcript with larger context windows (5-10 segments at a time) to catch cross-segment errors.

implementation.model: qwen2.5:1.5b via Ollama (1.18 GB Q4, best balance of speed and quality)

alternatives.flan-t5-large-grammar-synthesis: Grammar-specialized T5, ~60-150ms, but limited Ollama/GGUF support

implementation.vram_budget: RTX 3090 has 24GB. Whisper: 1-4GB. Correction model: 1.2GB. Plenty of headroom.
implementation.why_parakeet_benefits_most: Parakeet-TDT is CTC-based (no attention decoder for self-correction). Research shows LLM correction provides 68% relative WER reduction on CTC models vs minimal improvement on attention-based models like Whisper. Filler word removal is unique to LLM correction — no ASR model does this.

features.name: Push-to-Talk Director's Commentary
features.description: During a live meeting, the user presses a hotkey (e.g., holding Alt) and speaks a note only to the Tandem app. This audio is transcribed separately and injected into the AI context as a [Director's Note] and is visually distinguished in the transcript. Allows the user to verbally tag action items or leave breadcrumbs for the AI summary without having to type or disrupt the flow of the conversation.
steps: Phase 1 — Hotkey listener: register global shortcut (e.g., Alt/Cmd+Shift+Space) via Tauri globalShortcut plugin to activate 'Director mode'.
Phase 2 — Audio routing: when hotkey is held, capture default microphone stream, flag the resulting audio chunks in the pipeline as 'Director Note'.

Phase 3 — Transcript injection: insert the transcribed text into the live transcript with a special visual style (e.g., distinct background color, distinct icon) and an explicit [Director's Note] label.

Phase 4 — AI context handling: ensure this note is heavily weighted in the summary generation prompt (since it's explicit user instruction) but optionally excluded from plain PDF/text exports if the user wants separate clean notes.

features.name: Upgrade ASR Engine (Parakeet-TDT-1.1B + WER Research)
features.description: Evaluate and integrate the latest ASR models based on 2025-2026 WER research. Parakeet-TDT-1.1B achieves 1.39% WER on LibriSpeech (best open-source), 23x faster than Whisper large-v3. Combined with F035 (LLM correction), effective meeting WER should drop from ~11% to ~5-7%. This feature tracks the ASR engine upgrade path and benchmark validation.
steps: Phase 1 — Benchmark current setup: measure WER on a set of 5-10 saved meeting recordings using the existing Whisper/Parakeet pipeline. Establish baseline numbers for clean speech, noisy speech, and multi-speaker audio.

Phase 2 — Evaluate Parakeet-TDT-1.1B: download from HuggingFace, run same benchmark set. Compare WER + latency vs current 0.6B model. 1.1B requires ~4GB VRAM (fits alongside correction model on RTX 3090).

Phase 3 — Evaluate Canary-Qwen-2.5B: if accuracy is critical, test NVIDIA's SALM model (FastConformer encoder + Qwen3-1.7B decoder). 5.63% avg WER on diverse audio — best overall. Requires NeMo framework.
Phase 4 — Model selector in settings: let users choose ASR model (Whisper small/medium/large-v3-turbo, Parakeet 0.6B/1.1B, Canary). Auto-detect VRAM and recommend appropriate model.
Phase 5 — Streaming evaluation: test NVIDIA Nemotron-Speech-Streaming-EN-0.6B for real-time transcription with cache-aware architecture. Compare latency vs current chunked approach.
Phase 6 — Combined pipeline benchmark: measure WER of Parakeet-TDT-1.1B + Qwen2.5-1.5B correction (F035) end-to-end. Target: <6% WER on meeting audio, <2% on clean speech.

state_of_the_art_2026.best_speed: Parakeet-TDT-0.6B-v2: 3,380 RTFx (23x faster than Whisper large-v3)
state_of_the_art_2026.human_parity: 5.9% WER on Switchboard (Microsoft, 2016). Current models beat this on clean speech.

moonshine_27m.note: Matches Whisper Medium (28x larger), optimized for edge

key_techniques.tdt_transducer: Token-and-Duration Transducer decouples token/duration predictions, enabling 4-frame skip inference. Key to Parakeet's speed advantage.
key_techniques.salm_architecture: Speech-Augmented Language Model pairs ASR encoder with general-purpose LLM decoder (Canary-Qwen). Currently best accuracy.
key_techniques.llm_post_correction: 68% relative WER reduction on CTC-based models. Minimal improvement on attention-based models (Whisper). See F035.
key_techniques.speculative_decoding: SpecASR achieves 3-4x speedup on LLM-based ASR with zero accuracy loss.
key_techniques.cache_aware_streaming: NVIDIA Nemotron maintains state across audio chunks, avoiding repeated computation. Tunable latency/accuracy tradeoff.

practical_wer_floor.meeting_audio: ~5-8% on good audio, 15-25% with cross-talk and noise
practical_wer_floor.benchmark_to_production_gap: 2.8-5.7x degradation from benchmarks to real-world audio
practical_wer_floor.implication: Below ~4% WER, LLM correction and domain adaptation matter more than raw model improvements

research.recommendation_for_tandem: Parakeet-TDT-0.6B-v2 (or 1.1B if VRAM allows) + Qwen2.5-1.5B correction is optimal. Parakeet gives speed + accuracy, LLM fixes homophones/grammar/fillers. Target: <300ms total latency per segment, ~5-7% effective meeting WER.
papers: Whale: Multilingual ASR with w2v-BERT (arXiv:2506.01439, Jun 2025)
SpecASR: Speculative Decoding for ASR (arXiv:2507.18181, Jul 2025)
Moonshine: Tiny ASR for Edge (arXiv:2509.02523, Sep 2025)
Whisper Courtside: LLM Context for ASR (arXiv:2602.18966, Feb 2026)

features.name: Instant Fact Lookup Mid-Call
features.description: AI monitors the conversation and proactively surfaces relevant facts when topics come up. 'They just asked about our uptime — here's our SLA page.' Uses RAG over user-provided reference docs + web search. Facts appear in AI panel sidebar without interrupting the conversation flow.
steps: Phase 1 — Reference doc ingestion: drag-and-drop PDFs, URLs, or text files into a 'knowledge base' per meeting or globally. Chunk and embed locally (sentence-transformers or Ollama embeddings).
Phase 2 — Topic extraction: every 15s, extract key topics/entities from recent transcript. Compare against embedded knowledge base for relevant hits (cosine similarity > 0.7).
Phase 3 — Proactive surfacing: when a match is found, show a 'Fact Card' in the AI panel — source doc name, relevant excerpt, confidence score. Collapsible, dismissible.
Phase 4 — Web search fallback: if no local knowledge base hit, optionally search the web (via Brave/Tavily API) for the topic. User toggles this on/off.
Phase 5 — Learning loop: track which fact cards the user clicks/dismisses. Over time, improve relevance scoring per user.

features.name: Smart Follow-up Drafting
features.description: After a call ends, AI drafts a follow-up email/message based on the full transcript, action items, and decisions made. User reviews, edits, and sends directly or copies to clipboard. Supports templates for different follow-up styles (formal recap, casual check-in, proposal next steps).
steps: Phase 1 — Draft generation: after meeting ends, 'Draft Follow-up' button in summary view. LLM generates email from transcript + summary + action items.
Phase 2 — Template system: built-in templates (Meeting Recap, Action Items Only, Proposal Follow-up, Thank You). User can create custom templates with variable placeholders.
Phase 3 — Edit and send: rich text editor for the draft. Copy to clipboard, or send via mailto: link. Track which follow-ups were sent per meeting.
Phase 4 — Multi-recipient: detect participants from transcript (speaker diarization names). Generate personalized follow-ups per recipient with relevant-to-them highlights.
Phase 5 — Scheduled follow-ups: 'Remind me to follow up in 3 days if no response.' Local notification + pre-drafted nudge email.

features.name: Decision Logger
features.description: Automatically detect and log decisions made during calls. AI identifies statements like 'Let's go with option B', 'We agreed to...', 'The deadline is...' and tags them as decisions. Decisions get their own timeline view, searchable across all meetings. Never lose track of what was decided and when.
steps: Phase 1 — Decision detection: NLP classifier on transcript segments to identify decision statements. Use prompt-based classification with LLM — 'Is this a decision, action item, or neither?'
Phase 2 — Decision card UI: each detected decision shown as a card with timestamp, speaker, context (surrounding transcript), and confidence. User can confirm/dismiss/edit.
Phase 3 — Decision log view: new tab/section showing all decisions across meetings. Filter by date, participant, topic. Search full-text.
Phase 4 — Decision linking: link related decisions across meetings ('In Jan we decided X, but in March we changed to Y'). Show decision history per topic.
Phase 5 — Export: decisions as structured data (JSON, CSV) for project management tools. Webhook integration for auto-creating tickets from decisions.

features.name: Action Item Assignment and Tracking
features.description: Detect action items from calls ('I'll send the proposal by Friday'), assign owners, set due dates, and track completion. Dashboard shows all open action items across meetings. Integrates with the decision logger for a complete accountability trail.
steps: Phase 1 — Action item extraction: LLM prompt on transcript to extract action items with owner, due date, and description. Show inline during live transcript with 'task' icon.
Phase 2 — Assignment UI: action items appear in meeting summary with editable owner and due date fields. Auto-suggest owners from detected speaker names.
Phase 3 — Action item dashboard: new view showing all action items across all meetings. Filter by status (open/done/overdue), owner, date range. Sort by due date.
Phase 4 — Status tracking: mark items as done/in-progress. Show completion rate per meeting, per person. Local notifications for approaching due dates.
Phase 5 — Cross-meeting continuity: at start of follow-up meeting with same participants, surface open action items from previous meetings. 'Last time, Alice committed to X — is that done?'

features.name: Multi-Call Memory (Relationship Context)
features.description: AI remembers context across multiple calls with the same person/company. 'Last call with Acme Corp, they mentioned Q3 budget freeze — bring it up.' Builds a relationship graph over time. The AI co-pilot gets smarter with every interaction, like a teammate who was in every meeting.
steps: Phase 1 — Contact/company entity extraction: identify people and companies from transcripts using NER. Link meetings to contacts automatically.
Phase 2 — Relationship timeline: per-contact view showing all meetings, key topics discussed, decisions made, action items. Chronological timeline.
Phase 3 — Context injection: when starting a new meeting, AI panel auto-loads summary context from previous meetings with same contact. Shown as 'Previous context' card.
Phase 4 — Relationship insights: AI generates relationship health metrics — frequency of contact, sentiment trend, open commitments, topics that keep recurring.
Phase 5 — Smart suggestions: before a call, AI suggests topics to revisit based on relationship history. 'You discussed pricing 3 calls ago but never followed up.'

features.name: Document Reference (Drag-in PDFs and Files)
features.description: Drag PDFs, spreadsheets, or documents into the AI panel to give the AI instant context. 'Here's the contract — what are the key terms?' or 'Compare this proposal against what was discussed on the call.' Files are processed locally, never uploaded to cloud.

features.description: Export meeting outputs (summary, transcript, action items, decisions) using customizable templates. features.name: Async Handoff (Briefing Doc for Absent Teammates)
features.description: Generate a structured briefing document for teammates who missed the call. 'Here's what you missed and what you need to do.'
steps: Phase 1 — Handoff generation: after meeting ends, 'Create Handoff' button. User selects recipient(s) and their role/context. LLM generates personalized briefing.
Phase 2 — Recipient-aware filtering: briefing highlights only parts relevant to the recipient. Engineer gets technical decisions, manager gets timeline changes, designer gets UX feedback.
Phase 3 — Question flagging: identify moments where absent teammate was mentioned or questions were raised about their work. Flag these prominently in the handoff.
Phase 4 — Format options: generate as email draft, Slack message, or document. Copy to clipboard with formatting preserved.
Phase 5 — Handoff templates: customizable per team. Engineering handoff includes code references, sales handoff includes next steps and objections, executive handoff includes key metrics discussed.

features.name: Voice Commands for AI Panel
features.description: Control the AI panel with voice during calls via Ctrl+Space push-to-talk hotkey. Hold to listen, release to send. Wake word detection (OpenWakeWord ONNX pipeline) is built but dormant — needs custom 'Hey Tandem' model training. Currently using Alexa dev model as stand-in.

Phase 7 — Model training: train custom 'Hey Tandem' wake word model via openwakeword-trainer Docker pipeline. Ship melspectrogram.onnx + embedding_model.onnx + hey_tandem.onnx.
Phase 8 — End-to-end testing: record, say wake word / press Ctrl+Space, verify full pipeline from audio tap → ONNX inference / hotkey → Tauri event → UI response → AI command execution.

features.name: Transcription Quality Improvements
features.description: Improve Whisper transcription accuracy through audio pipeline optimizations and parameter tuning

sub_features.name: Buffer VAD segments to minimum 3 seconds
sub_features.description: Accumulate VAD speech segments in a buffer before sending to Whisper. Short chunks (<3s) produce poor transcription quality. Buffer flushes when >= 3s of audio is accumulated or after a 2-second silence gap.
steps: Add transcription_buffer, transcription_buffer_start_ts, transcription_buffer_last_activity fields to AudioPipeline struct
Replace direct VAD segment sends with buffer accumulation (append to Vec<f32>)
Flush buffer to Whisper when >= 48000 samples (3s at 16kHz)
Add silence-gap detection: flush partial buffer after 2s of no new VAD speech
Update flush_remaining_audio() to drain buffer on recording stop

sub_features.name: Set temperature to 0.0 with automatic fallback
sub_features.description: Use greedy decoding (temperature 0.0) for deterministic output. Whisper's built-in entropy_thold fallback retries with higher temperatures only when needed.

sub_features.name: Flip suppress_non_speech_tokens to false
sub_features.description: whisper.cpp changed the default to false because true paradoxically causes end-of-segment hallucinations ('Thank you for watching', 'Amen', etc.).

sub_features.name: Add initial_prompt for meeting context
sub_features.description: Set a meeting-oriented initial_prompt to bias Whisper toward business vocabulary. Feed previous segment output as context for continuity.

sub_features.name: Expand hallucination post-filter
sub_features.description: Add more hallucination patterns, compression ratio check, and language sanity check to the existing clean_repetitive_text() filter.

features.name: Session-Aware HUD + Branch Stamping
features.description: Lower-friction project routing in solo mode. The solo HUD picker shows live Claude Code sessions (from the local ~/.claude/sessions registry) with project folder, current branch, and last-activity time; clicking one switches to that project, auto-registering unknown paths. Every project switch, session_start feed entry, and task handoff is stamped with the git branch (resolved from .git/HEAD incl. worktree indirection, no git spawn), and a calm warning fires when the checkout branch differs from the branch the Claude session sees. Privacy: only the last 64KB of a transcript is read and only gitBranch/cwd/type/timestamp keys are extracted; never auto-switches without a click. F061 addition (virtual sub-projects keyed by chat session): a project row gains an optional nullable session_id; picking a live session activates or creates a virtual sub-project with identity (path, session_id) named after the chat title, so several chats against ONE folder each become their own Tandem project. Its notes/transcripts/tasks/feed file under <path>/.tandem/sessions/<session_id>/ instead of the folder root, so filings from different chats never mix. A plain folder project may coexist at the same path. Uniqueness moved from path-unique to a (path, COALESCE(session_id,'')) unique index; the Rust candidate matcher prefers the session-specific project over the plain one. Filing tolerates the session folder being manually deleted (recreated on write); cleanup is manual.

features.name: Typed Transcript Notes (Solo Mode)
features.description: A compact, keyboard-first note input in the recording view lets the user type a quick note or link that is injected INTO the live transcript as a first-class segment marked source="note" (Enter to add, verbatim/link-safe). Because it lands in TranscriptContext state, it flows through every existing transcript consumer with no new plumbing: the live transcript view, the saved meeting transcript (Rust SQLite via api_save_transcript, source persisted to the speaker column, no schema change), the .tandem/live-transcript.md that Claude Code /loop reads (rendered as "Note: ..."), @code task files, and LLM summaries. Notes render with a distinct indigo "Note" badge (dark-mode variants) in both the live view and meeting-details (shared VirtualizedTranscriptView) and skip filler-word cleanup so links survive. Pure logic (marker/timestamp/ordering) in transcriptNotes.ts with 14 vitest cases; note sequence_ids live in a high namespace (>=1e9) so they never collide with the worker counter (which would drop a real segment via dedup).

features.name: Handover Document (no-AI post-recording export)
features.description: After a recording, alongside "Generate Summary", the user can produce a HANDOVER.md: a verbatim, deterministic record of the call rather than an AI interpretation. It interleaves four streams on the recording clock: transcript segments, typed notes, screenshots (embedded inline as images with folder-relative paths) and clipboard captures (fenced so pasted code survives). Links the user typed or copied are lifted into a Links section at the top with their timestamps, because that is what people come back for; links merely spoken are excluded since transcription mangles them. Works in Solo mode specifically: Solo has no jot store and files typed lines straight into the transcript marked source="note" (F062), so notes arrive as transcript segments and are split back out by that marker. Needs no model and no network, so it stays available when summary generation is blocked or no provider is configured.
